revised.disagreements: comment and docstring only, naming the segment-qualified reasons. The junction oracle's prose cited reference_anchor_unresolved and anchor_removed, the spellings this branch replaced with <segment>_<reason>. No comparison, tolerance or branch in the oracle changed -- it does not read the reasons list at all; the strings appear only in the explanation of why a null junction window is an identity rather than a skip.
revised.MECHANISMS: the assay.ambiguous_calls row lost its truth_gap and gained n_ambiguous_bases in truth_fields, because the count is now exported. The catalogue enforces field ownership at collection, so this row had to change before any test could declare the field. No other row was touched and no mechanism was added or removed.
revised.test_the_coverage_report_numbers_are_pin: the coverage pin moved assay.ambiguous_calls from gap-limited to verified, and the distribution from 20 verified / 5 gap-limited to 21 / 4. The row moved because the gap closed -- n_ambiguous_bases is exported -- which is the first row on this branch to move by the truth arriving rather than by a test being registered. The narrative docstring gained a paragraph saying so and the realized-not-requested semantics. The pin is strictly as strong: still per mechanism, still 31 rows, still asserting the distribution alongside, so a swap cannot hide in it.
revised.test_a_truth_gap_stays_visible_even_when: docstring only; the assertion is unchanged and still iterates every mechanism declaring a truth gap. The worked example named assay.ambiguous_calls as the live case of a mechanism verified on a borrowed field while its own truth went unexported. That is no longer true of it, so the example was retargeted to junction.n_addition, which is still in exactly that state: the junction bases are checkable against the sequence but the record does not say how many TdT added. An example has to be a mechanism that is still in the state being described.
revised.untemplated_runs: classification substrate changed from letter case to the engine's per-base flags, newly exposed as p_nucleotide_mask and tdt_addition_mask. The run splitting is unchanged and still delegates to provenance.untemplated_runs; only the P/N/mixed label is derived differently. Strictly stronger, and measurably so: over 200 human IGH records the case version reported 382 pure-N runs on recombine() alone but 328 N and 54 mixed once sequencing_errors(count=8) was added, inventing palindromes the recombination never wrote. The flag version reports 382 N in all three configurations tested, including under hypermutation. An oracle whose answer moves because a later pass rewrote the display encoding was reporting the encoding, not the provenance.
revised.REPORTS: one key renamed, split_by_case -> split_by_origin, following the function. The registry maps every public function in the module to the identities it can report disagreements on; this entry is () in both versions because the function supplies material to another comparison rather than reporting one itself. No identity was added, removed or retargeted.
revised._assert_counts_realized_not_drawn: the three-base replacement draw. A substitution drew its replacement from all four bases including the one already at the site, so about a quarter of draws wrote back what was there; such a write changes nothing and was correctly not counted, which left `mutate(model="uniform")`, `pcr_amplify` and `sequencing_errors` delivering ~76% of their configured count. The draw now excludes the base at the site, so realized equals requested. This helper's third assertion was `sum(changed) < draws`, with its own comment saying why: the shortfall was what told a realized count apart from a drawn one on this fixture. The shortfall is gone, so the assertion is inverted to `sum(changed) == draws` -- not weakened but repointed, and it now fails if the four-base draw ever returns. The per-record equality above it, which is the load-bearing claim and compares the counter against a cross-run count of changed positions, is untouched. What the inversion does cost is the evidence that the counter is not simply the drawn count; that is replaced by a new Rust test, `pcr_error_count_is_what_was_applied_not_what_was_drawn`, covering the one configuration where the two still differ -- a permissive contract that admits no replacement anywhere leaves a requested error undelivered.

The draw now excludes the base at the site, so realized equals requested. Registration text only in the body's own terms: the @verifies claim no longer says a replacement is drawn from all four bases. Same records, same cross-run basis, same assertions -- which live in `_assert_counts_realized_not_drawn`, declared above.

revised.test_every_counted_mutation_changed_a_ba: the three-base replacement draw. The prose described the no-op draw as current behaviour and recorded the measurement that went with it (46 of 200 records realising no mutation); all 200 realise one now, and the subtraction the docstring describes remains in the engine as the backstop for the write paths that pin their value rather than draw it.
revised.test_no_bundled_s5f_kernel_draws_the_bas: the three-base replacement draw. A substitution drew its replacement from all four bases including the one already at the site, so about a quarter of draws wrote back what was there; such a write changes nothing and was correctly not counted, which left `mutate(model="uniform")`, `pcr_amplify` and `sequencing_errors` delivering ~76% of their configured count. The prose said S5F was the exception to the uniform model's no-op rate, which is no longer a distinction between them. Rewritten to say what the test is still for: S5F reaches this through the shipped tables rather than through a guard -- the sampler takes every positive entry in a substitution row, and the four bundled tables carry zero on the row's own centre base -- so a table shipped with a positive diagonal would make this model an attempt budget again and no other test would notice.
revised._all_records_have_migrated_prefix: docstring only, one word: it said "used by the full-stack golden test" and that test is now `test_full_stack_replay_round_trips_through_a_trace_file` -- see replaced['test_full_stack_replay_reproduces_committed_golden_trace']. The predicate is unchanged and still returns whether every trace record falls under a migrated prefix.
revised._tsv: Takes the fixture's variant name instead of a `mixed` Boolean. The fixtures stopped being 'plain or the mixed-features one' when two more variants were added to cover the mutation and corruption passes, which no golden exercised. Same body otherwise: write the TSV, read it back.
revised.test_one_seed_produces_identical_bytes_t: The parameter it passes through is now a variant name rather than a Boolean. The claim, the assertion and what it compares are unchanged, and it now runs over six fixtures instead of four.
revised.test_output_matches_the_committed_golden: As above -- parameter shape only. The golden files themselves were regenerated in this branch because per-pass substreams change every seeded draw; the comparison that reads them is untouched.
revised.golden_name: Builds the filename from a variant name rather than from a fixed `_mixed_features` suffix. The three plain fixtures keep their existing names exactly, which is why the committed plain goldens are regenerated in place rather than renamed.
revised._experiment: Applies the variant's builder calls from the VARIANTS table instead of hard-coding `invert_d` + `receptor_revision` behind a Boolean. The mixed-features variant produces the identical experiment it did before.
revised.write_reproducibility_tsv: `mixed: bool` became `variant: str`. The body still compiles the experiment and writes one TSV.
revised.every_fixture: Returns `(name, locus, n, variant)` built from the FIXTURE_SPECS table, where it previously built `(name, locus, n, mixed)` from the loci plus one hard-coded mixed entry. Two fixtures are added, none removed, and the four existing tuples are the same configurations under the new shape.
revised.test_a_pass_configured_off_is_the_same_a: The `zero_differs` branch is gone, so the assertion is unconditional. It existed for one pass -- `invert_d(prob=0.0)`, whose coin flip fell between the two NP generations on the shared stream and re-drew NP2 -- and per-pass substreams removed that exception. This is a STRENGTHENING: the branch it lost was the one that accepted a difference.
revised.test_the_library_prep_passes_leave_the_r: Docstring only. The group it asserts over fell from eight passes to seven because `polymerase_indels` was measured moving np1_length/np2_length and had to declare them, which puts the `>= 7` threshold at its floor; the docstring now says so. The assertion is unchanged, and it is now tight: the next pass that declares anything fails it.
revised.Pass: Lost the `zero_differs` field. It recorded, with a measurement, a pass whose off switch was not equivalent to absence; `invert_d` was the only one, per-pass substreams fixed it, and a declaration mechanism with no declarations is a permission nobody checks. The measurement itself is kept in that pass's `notes`.
revised.PASSES: Two entries changed. `invert_d` drops `np2_length` from `may_move` and drops `zero_differs`: with its own substream the pass no longer re-draws NP2, measured 0 fields moved over 200 records at prob=0.0, and the non-vacuity half of the isolation test fails on a declaration that is no longer exercised. `polymerase_indels` gains `np1_length`/`np2_length`, which is a finding rather than a design change: the record reports the untemplated span the molecule has rather than the bases TdT added, so an indel landing in an NP region moves it by one. Measured on the engine as it was, before this branch: 9 of the first 20 seeds move them. The comparison runs on seed 17, which put no indel in an NP region, so the substream change did not break this -- it stopped hiding it.
revised.check_record: The claim that the first and last segment span the whole molecule is now conditioned on the scenario's `indels` flag, and bounded rather than exact when indels are on. An insertion can land outside every segment -- before the V's first base or past the J's last -- and the equality held only because no seed had drawn that case; per-pass substreams moved where the indels land and one record of 300 did. The bound is the indels no per-segment counter claims, so it is exact when every indel is inside a segment, and the no-indel scenarios keep the unconditional equality.

test_the_reason_counts_one_unresolved_an.why: the pin recorded the limitation this branch removes. It asserted that reference_anchor_unresolved appears once per unresolved anchor and stated, in its docstring, that the record does NOT say which anchor -- the count was information and the attribution was missing. The successor asserts the attribution: the set of segments the reasons name equals the set whose allele is unresolved, and the unqualified spelling is gone from the vocabulary. Same records, same 200-record draw, strictly more pinned.

test_the_pass_with_no_counter_of_its_own.why: the predecessor asserted that ambiguous_base_calls moves no counter at all, because assay.ambiguous_calls declared a truth gap: the masking count lived in the trace as corrupt.ns.count and nowhere in the record. Its own failure message instructed this change -- 'assay.ambiguous_calls no longer declares a truth gap, so its count may now be exported -- in which case this test should check it moves'. n_ambiguous_bases is now exported, so the successor asserts the positive: exactly n_ambiguous_bases moves and no other owned counter, and its value equals the number of positions that actually differ from the unmasked run on the same seed. Strictly more pinned -- the predecessor could not distinguish a correct zero from a counter that had stopped reporting.

split_by_case.why: same partition, honest substrate. The predecessor split an untemplated run into its P and N parts by letter case, which is the convention at the moment the recombination writes a base and not afterwards: sequencing_errors lowercases what it corrupts and hypermutation writes uppercase, so case stops naming the origin as soon as either runs. The successor reads the engine's p_nucleotide_mask. It takes the simulation as a parameter because the answer lives there rather than in the run's bytes, and it is renamed because a function called split_by_case that no longer splits by case is a trap for the next reader. Nothing outside this module's own REPORTS registry called it.

test_pcr_substitution_base_distribution_.why: the three-base replacement draw. A substitution drew its replacement from all four bases including the one already at the site, so about a quarter of draws wrote back what was there; such a write changes nothing and was correctly not counted, which left `mutate(model="uniform")`, `pcr_amplify` and `sequencing_errors` delivering ~76% of their configured count. The draw now excludes the base at the site, so realized equals requested. This predecessor asserted the MARGINAL over A/C/G/T is uniform at 0.25 each, which cannot hold once the draw is conditional, and not because of a defect: on its own fixture `A` occupies 6 of the 15 templated positions, so `A` is the base most often excluded and its marginal falls to a measured 0.2096. The successor asserts the conditional claim the model actually makes -- given the base at the site, the replacement is uniform over the other three and never that base -- from a transition table built by pairing each error's recorded site with its recorded base, restricted to single-error records at a position the fixture fixes. Measured 1,276 samples, four rows of 482/265/284/245, diagonal empty. Strictly stronger: the marginal test would have passed a draw that sometimes wrote the incumbent and spread the remainder evenly.

test_full_stack_replay_reproduces_commit.why: the committed golden it compared against is the compat suite's frozen anchor, and regenerating it was the wrong way to settle a deliberate model change. The predecessor compared a live run at seed 4242 against `tests/golden/trace_files/full_stack_seed4242.trace.json`, so it fails whenever a sampling model changes on purpose -- the three-base replacement draw did exactly that, moving `corrupt.pcr.error_base[0]`. Regenerating the file would have destroyed what `test_v1_fixtures_exist_in_committed_set` and `test_v1_fixture_has_no_v2_fields_serialised` exist to protect: a fixture written by an older build, which is the only way to prove v1 -> current compatibility at the next schema bump. The successor keeps every assertion the predecessor made about the replay -- the migrated-prefix check, the signature comparison, the length and per-choice address+value equality under the drained cursor -- and takes them against a file it writes to a temporary directory itself, so there is no committed artifact to go stale. It also adds `assert a_choices`, which the predecessor lacked: an empty trace satisfied every comparison in it. Durability of the frozen artifacts stays with `test_trace_file_compat.py`, which already loads them, parses every address and replays them record for record; cross-platform determinism of the values stays with `tests/acceptance/test_reproducibility.py`.

test_an_off_pass_keeps_the_rearrangement.why: The old test asserted that an off pass DOES shift the draws behind it -- `same_sequence == 0` over 40 records -- because the engine held one random stream for the whole plan. Its own docstring said that if per-pass substreams were ever added the sequence half would start passing and the test should be replaced by the stronger claim. They were. The successor asserts the opposite and more: every exported field identical, molecule included, on every record. Renamed because the old name states the old behaviour.

test_the_one_pass_whose_off_switch_is_no.why: It pinned `invert_d(prob=0.0)` re-drawing NP2 at exactly the precision of that finding, and said in its own docstring that if the finding were ever fixed the test and the declaration should both be deleted. Fixed: with its own substream the pass moves nothing at prob=0.0, measured over 200 records. The claim is now covered, unconditionally and for every pass with an off switch, by the parametrized test named above -- which previously had a branch that exempted this one.

allow.dead-code: `FULL_STACK_GOLDEN` in tests/components/io/test_trace_replay.py, and the `from tests.support import paths` import that existed only to build it. The one test that read the constant no longer reads a committed artifact -- see replaced['test_full_stack_replay_reproduces_committed_golden_trace'] -- so the constant named a file this module no longer touches. The file itself is untouched and still read by tests/components/io/test_trace_file_compat.py, which is the suite the durability contract belongs to. Also `MIXED_LOCUS`, `MIXED_N` and `MIXED_NAME` in tests/support/golden.py: three constants that described the single non-plain fixture back when there was one. The fixture table that replaced them (`VARIANTS` + `FIXTURE_SPECS`) describes four variants, and a per-variant constant does not generalise -- see revised['every_fixture']. The mixed-features fixture itself is still generated and still checked, under the same filename.
